task.description:
WF-03 Step 3d -- IDIOM/INTEGRITY GATE on the ISS-0109 implementation. Review the DIFF:
`git diff 70736d5..HEAD -- test/` (the new helper test/support/tenant_fixture.ex plus its adoption
in test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs).

SECURITY-REVIEWER has already PASSed this diff (step-03c) with per-invariant verdicts, and
verified INV-F-8 query-by-query and INV-F-9 interpolation-site-by-site. Do not redo that work.

Your standard scope applies: idiomatic Elixir/OTP usage, supervision integrity, scope creep,
decision-record consistency. The gate-approved design is lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md (passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR
at bf87afb, plus two ORCH label corrections at 4a20f7a).

FOUR SPECIFIC THINGS THIS RUN NEEDS YOU TO RULE ON. Three are ELIXIR-DEV's own flagged MINORs
where it deliberately did NOT decide unilaterally; the fourth is scope.

RULING 1 (the important one) -- A REAL INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN THE GATE-APPROVED DESIGN,
which neither CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR pass caught. SS3.2 types registration_present? and
schema_present? as boolean(). SS3.5 -- which INV-F-4 explicitly names as normative for
capture_schema_state/1's failure boundary -- requires a scalar whose query failed to degrade to
nil. Both cannot hold. ELIXIR-DEV implemented SS3.5 (boolean() | nil, where false means
observed-absent and nil means not-observed) and documented it in the moduledoc. Rule on this
explicitly: is implementing the normative section the right resolution, and is the resulting
@type/@spec surface coherent? Note the substantive argument in favour, and check it rather than
accept it: taking SS3.2's literal boolean() would report an UNOBSERVED schema as ABSENT, which is
precisely the observed-vs-unobserved conflation SS3.5 exists to forbid, and a capture report that
says "schema absent" when it simply failed to look would be worse than no report -- it would have
re-created ISS-0109's original misdiagnosis in a new place. If you agree, say so and ORCH will
have the design's SS3.2 corrected to match. If you disagree, this is a FAIL and the code changes
instead.

RULING 2 -- SS3.6 asks the teardown line to carry the owning test module/name, but the normative
five-key opts carry no ExUnit context and ExUnit exposes no public "current test" API (it lives
under the ExUnit.Runner key in the module-runner process's dictionary, not the test process's).
ELIXIR-DEV's owning_test/0 walks the OTP-25+ :parent chain, the same shape as ExUnit's own
safe_pdict_current/1, and degrades to "unknown" rather than ever failing a teardown. Rule on
whether reaching into another process's dictionary via the :parent chain is acceptable idiom HERE
(test-only helper, best-effort log enrichment, degrades safely) or whether it is the kind of
private-internals coupling that will silently break on an ExUnit change. If the latter, say what
the code should do instead -- note that the marker, the phase and schema_present_before_drop do
NOT depend on it, so dropping the field entirely is an available answer.

RULING 3 -- tables_present deliberately excludes schema_migrations (its contents are captured
separately as applied_versions), matching expected_tenant_tables/0, so SS3.3's oracle-rot test
stays a plain both-direction set equality with no filtering on TEST-DESIGNER's side. Confirm this
is consistent and that the oracle-rot guard specified in the design still works against the
implementation as written.

RULING 4 -- SCOPE. Confirm the diff does not creep beyond the design: exactly one new test-only
module, adoption in exactly the two modules ISS-0109 names, no touch to the other 39 copy-paste
sites (ISS-0112/GH#366), no production change (INV-F-2), drop_schema!/1 still present in
promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs for its unrelated SandboxPool caller at :463. Also confirm the
helper does not quietly absorb any of ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113 or ISS-0107.

ALSO CHECK, as ordinary idiom review of a 630-line new module: naming, @spec accuracy against
actual return shapes, the guarded/rescue structure (SECURITY-REVIEWER noted five bare
`%{rows: _} =` matches reached only through guarded/2 or an outer rescue -- confirm that holds as
IDIOM, not just as safety), no dead code, no copy-paste from the very template this helper exists
to replace, and that a test-only module living in test/support/ genuinely does not need a
supervision-tree presence (compare test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex, which made the same call
deliberately and documents why).

CARRY-FORWARD, do not act on: SECURITY-REVIEWER recorded one non-blocking MINOR -- the failure
paths log raw Exception.message(exception) at tenant_fixture.ex:274 and :382, which is bounded
today (every query that can raise is tenant-scoped) but where a DBConnection.ConnectionError
message could include host:port. It recommended carrying this into ISS-0112/GH#366 rather than
expanding this run. ORCH will do that. Mention it only if you think that judgement is wrong.

CONSTRAINTS: you gate, you do not edit. On FAIL, name each gap specifically so rework is narrow.
Toolchain: plain `mix compile` only (Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 vs a 1.18.3-otp-27 pin, ISS-0106, filed
and not yours) -- no --warnings-as-errors, no `mix format`. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by
explicit filename, never `git add -A`. Note ORCH may have handoffs/orchestrator.log modified in
the working tree -- that file is ORCH's, leave it alone and fetch rather than pulling if a rebase
refuses.
acceptance_criteria: RULING 1 is given explicitly: whether implementing SS3.5's normative nil-degradation over SS3.2's literal boolean() is the correct resolution of the design's internal contradiction, and whether the resulting @type/@spec surface is coherent
RULING 2 is given explicitly: whether owning_test/0's :parent-chain process-dictionary walk is acceptable idiom for this test-only best-effort log field, or what it should do instead
RULING 3 is given explicitly: that excluding schema_migrations from tables_present is consistent and that SS3.3's oracle-rot guard still works against the implementation as written

RULING 4 is given explicitly: no scope creep -- one new test-only module, exactly two adopted modules, no production change, drop_schema!/1 retained for its SandboxPool caller, and none of ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113/0107 quietly absorbed

Ordinary idiom review of the new module is reported: naming, @spec accuracy against actual return shapes, the guarded/rescue structure as idiom, absence of dead code, and no supervision-tree need (compared against test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's documented precedent)
Decision-record consistency is checked -- no docs/migration/decisions/ record and no gate-approved design record is contradicted by the implementation
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated; on FAIL each gap is named specifically enough for narrow rework
